cands.bio: Democrat and Birmingham police sergeant who has served in the Alabama House, District 55, since winning a 2023 special election to succeed Fred Plump Jr. Has worked as a school resource officer and on a public housing task force. Holds degrees from Miles College and Oakland City University.

endorsements.text: In his 2023 special election, endorsed by House Minority Leader Anthony Daniels (D) and Birmingham Mayor Randall Woodfin.
Wikipedia also reports his 2023 endorsements from multiple Democratic state lawmakers and officials, including Anthony Daniels and Randall Woodfin.

cands.gaps: We found no stated positions or official actions by Hendrix on data centers, homestead property taxes, limits on outside buyers of land, growth and land protection, immigration or H-1B, foreign or big-donor money, guns, abortion, or school choice. The list of bills he has sponsored was empty on the page we read, so no specific legislation could be tied to him. His campaign platform covers economic growth, public safety, education, broadband and lowering the grocery tax in general terms only. He did not complete Ballotpedia's 2023 or 2026 candidate surveys, and his only survey answers date from 2022. We found no documented controversies, foreign ties or notable endorsements for the 2026 race. His exact year of arrival in Alabama is not needed, since he reports being born and raised in Birmingham.

qual.background: Alabama House member for District 55 since 2023 (about three years); Birmingham Police sergeant, former school resource officer, and member of a public housing task force; master's degree in Strategic Management.
qual.why: He has held a legislative seat for about three years and has a long public-safety career plus a management degree, which puts him in the upper-middle range. His record shows no budget or policy career and no chamber leadership role, and committee seats are not counted.
